movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Used mainly for balance, generally kept controlled and close to body
movement_profile.difficulty: Beginner to advanced depending on complexity of steps and spins
movement_profile.footwork: Alternating kicks forward with feet, rotational pivots on supporting foot, fast jumps timed to beat
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Danced solo, duo side-by-side or facing, or in synchronized groups
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Minimal torso movement, hips follow leg kicks subtly
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Beginners start with basic steps; advanced dancers add spins and aerial jumps
movement_profile.partnering: Duo-kick involves facing partner and tapping feet; physical contact otherwise avoided
movement_profile.posture: Relatively stiff upper body with slight knee bend for jumps

signature_moves.description: Five quick alternating kicks forward and backward
signature_moves.name: Basic 5-touch step

signature_moves.description: Rotational turn on one foot, sometimes airborne
signature_moves.name: Spin

signature_moves.description: High energetic jump with forward kick
signature_moves.name: Jump kick

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Energetic, fast-paced with precise timing to 140–160 BPM music
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid uncoordinated foot contact with others except in duo-kick; maintain balance to prevent injury

music_profile.musical_form: Minimal melodic arrangement with emphasis on rhythm and bass
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Four-on-the-floor 909 kick drum with offbeat elements
music_profile.sound_description: Jumpstyle music features a steady, driving four-on-the-floor 909 kick drum at 140–160 BPM, layered with pitched basslines and square wave synthesizers. The sound is minimal yet energetic, with rhythmic offbeats and melodic elements drawn from hardstyle and techno hardcore.
music_profile.vocal_style: Typically instrumental; some tracks include sampled or minimal vocals

basic_steps: Stand with feet together, knees slightly bent
Jump and kick right foot forward while left foot stays grounded
Jump and switch feet, left foot forward, right foot grounded
Add rotational footwork by pivoting on supporting foot
Incorporate arm movements for balance, keeping upper body stiff
teaching.formation: Solo, duo (side-by-side or facing), or group synchronized dancing
teaching.level_notes: Start with oldschool 5-touch basic steps, progress to hardjump 6-touch steps, then ownstyle with spins and freestyle elements
teaching.rhythm: Four-on-the-floor kick drum pattern at 140–160 BPM
